cases.name: Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc.
UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc.

profile_text.body:
Suno is a for-profit startup founded in 2022 and headquartered in Cambridge, MA, that operates an AI music generation platform at suno.com. The company describes its tool as an AI song generator capable of producing complete original songs, including vocals, lyrics, and full production, from a single text prompt in under a minute, across any genre. A free tier is available, while paid tiers add higher output limits and additional features: the Pro plan offers 500 songs per month, royalty-free music, commercial use rights, stem separation, audio uploads of up to 8 minutes, and access to what the company calls its best and most personalized model, v5.5, and the Premier plan offers 2,000 songs per month along with Suno Studio, which the company describes as a first-of-its-kind web-based generative audio workstation combining traditional DAW functionality with AI-powered creation, plus a multitrack editor, MIDI export, and persona voices.

Suno faces substantial litigation tied to its AI training and output practices. Major recorded music companies, including UMG Recordings and Sony Music, filed suit against Suno in the District of Massachusetts, and a series of additional cases have been brought in courts across Massachusetts, New York, Texas, and Illinois, including actions filed by individual plaintiffs and by S.A. Jamendo, as well as cases styled Gawronski v. Suno, Rugnetta v. Suno, Pilavian v. Suno, Reyna v. Suno, Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, and Woulard v. Suno. The volume and variety of these cases reflect the broader industry disputes over copyright and intellectual property provenance in AI-generated music.
